feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The salute is an embodied action, not a static object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — A deliberate human-invented form of symbolic behavior.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — No inspiration from biology or natural mimicry.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Performed manually without energy systems.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Provides no physical support or load-bearing function.
feedback.Observable: Included — Must be visually perceived to function as intended.
feedback.Physical Medium: Included — Requires a human body for performance; no gesture exists without a medium.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires human initiation; not autonomously active.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Developed to encode recognition, submission, or solidarity.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Included — Visibly outputs meaning through a choreographed motion.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Does not process input or logic.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Does not internally transform itself; expressive only.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — A person-to-person act of recognition or acknowledgment.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Symbolically important but not a technical system component.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Always requires human intentionality to exist.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Systems can operate without it, though symbolically diminished.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Represents institutional respect, duty, and relational roles.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Visually communicates acknowledgement and hierarchy.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Precisely defined in military manuals, including angle, posture, timing.
feedback.Compositional: Excluded — The gesture is atomic and indivisible.
feedback.Normative: Included — Expected and socially policed in relevant institutional contexts.
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not reference itself or abstract categories.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Structured through phases in time (raise, hold, lower).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Excluded — It is physical and embodied, not virtual.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists entirely through shared institutional understanding.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Formally specified by military codes and handbooks.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Communicates role, rank, and membership status.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Governed by formal codes of military conduct.
feedback.Economically Significant: Excluded — Not directly involved in value generation.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Represents allegiance, nationalism, and sometimes political symbolism.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Repeated in highly patterned, ceremonial formats.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Tied to moral ideas of respect, duty, and loyalty.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the military salute as a codified, symbolic, and ritualized embodied gesture. Its identity depends on institutional rules, social meaning, and precise performance. It is defined as a time-based communicative act embedded in cultural and political frameworks.
